summary: The incident was caused by a sudden CPU‑bound resource exhaustion in market-data-service, which drove its request latency from ~40 ms to ~1800 ms. Pricing-engine, which depends on market-data-service, timed out on each quote computation, producing the observed deadline‑exceeded errors.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource exhaustion in market-data-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A CPU‑bound spike in market-data-service caused its request latency to rise sharply, which in turn triggered deadline‑exceeded errors in pricing‑engine.

causal_chain.claim: CPU usage surge → latency spike in market-data-service

ranked_hypotheses.title: Pricing-engine internal processing slowdown
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Pricing-engine itself became CPU‑bound or deadlocked, causing it to miss its internal deadline regardless of market-data-service latency.
assumptions: pricing-engine CPU metrics would show a spike
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Contradicted by stable request rate, lack of any deployment or config change, and strong evidence of upstream latency.

facts.statement: Pricing-engine deadline errors began shortly after market-data-service latency spiked.
CPU usage and latency spikes co‑occurred, while request volume stayed constant.
No recent code or config changes could have introduced a regression.

timeline.event: market-data-service latency p99 jumps to ~1 s (avg 977 ms, max 1979 ms)
Continued deadline errors and high latency

recommended_actions.action: Investigate market-data-service CPU usage (e.g., thread pool saturation, GC pauses) and apply appropriate scaling or optimisation.
recommended_actions.rationale: CPU spike is the root cause of latency and downstream timeouts.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on market-data-service latency and CPU thresholds to catch similar spikes earlier.
recommended_actions.rationale: Early detection can prevent downstream impact on pricing-engine.

recommended_actions.action: Review market-data-service code paths for potential CPU‑intensive queries triggered at ~13:20 (e.g., market‑wide data refresh).
recommended_actions.rationale: Identify the specific operation causing the CPU burst.

data_gaps: No CPU/memory metrics for pricing-engine to rule out local overload.
No detailed trace data linking individual pricing-engine requests to market-data-service latency.
No internal logs from market-data-service beyond errors (none found).

findings.statement: pricing-engine emitted ERROR logs "quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms" starting at 2026-04-09T13:23:57Z and continuing every few seconds.
market-data-service p99 latency spiked from ~40 ms to ~1800 ms, with a bucket at 2026-04-09T13:20:00Z showing avg 977 ms, max 1979.98 ms.
market-data-service CPU usage rose sharply, reaching avg 90.89 % and max 94.51 % at 2026-04-09T13:24:00Z.
market-data-service request rate remained stable (~950 req/s) throughout the incident window.
No deployments were recorded for pricing-engine or market-data-service on 2026‑04‑09.
No configuration or feature‑flag changes were made for any service in the incident window.
market-data-service emitted no WARN/ERROR logs containing the word "error" during the window.
